chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Sadqah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard my father saying: When the owner of the net strikes with the net, whatever it catches in it, whether living or dead, is permissible, except that which has no shell. And the floating fish is not to be eaten, because the meaning in this report is what we said in the earlier reports: it is the same whether the dead one is distinguished from the living one, in which case it is permissible for him to eat all of them; but if they are distinguished, then it is not permissible, according to what we have previously presented.

key_terms.الطَّافِي: the floating one (fish that died in water)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating fish that died in the water but were caught in the net?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying the permissibility of mixed catches, emphasizing that the general rule allows consuming both living and dead fish unless the dead ones are distinctly identifiable. This ruling specifically excludes 'floating fish' (*al-taffah*) from consumption, a distinction rooted in the principle that clearly dead aquatic creatures are not halal, whereas those caught alive or indistinguishably mixed remain permissible. This hadith serves as a key juristic basis for distinguishing between *taharah* (purity) and *halal* status in marine life within Shia fiqh.
